_comment: A flock is capital before it is meat: wool every season, milk through spring and summer, and only slaughtered when there is a surplus or nothing else to eat.
name: sheep
label: Sheep

_comment: Red deer. They belong to nobody, they move where the grazing is, and a hunted one is gone - so a country carries only so many, and hunters who take them all have taken them all.
name: deer
label: Deer

_comment: Wild pig. Bad-tempered, quick to breed, and worth the risk: more meat off one than off a deer.
name: boar
label: Wild boar

_comment: Wolves have to eat too. They take what they can catch - deer, boar, and a sheep nobody is watching - and a pup taken young becomes the dog that keeps them off.
name: wolf
label: Wolf

_comment: A tamed wolf, raised to the flock. It keeps the sheep together and the wolves off them, which is the difference between a shepherd watching a flock and a shepherd chasing one.
name: shepherd_dog
label: Shepherd dog
